phases.title: Approvals & accounts
phases.blurb: Nothing goes live without Clayton's OK. Accounts must be in his name.

phases.title: Launch the site
phases.blurb: Domain, hosting, email, forms, analytics. Preview first, cutover only after approval.

phases.title: Claim and unify the brand
phases.blurb: Close the gaps (X, Facebook Page, TikTok) and make every profile point at the site.

phases.title: Data & content
phases.blurb: Feed the site real numbers and real copy.

phases.title: Growth
phases.blurb: More eyes on the rips, more buyers on eBay.

phases.title: Retention
phases.blurb: Turn one-time eBay buyers into a list, a Want List and repeat customers.

phases.title: Ongoing
phases.blurb: Short routines that keep it all alive.

tasks.title: Research the brand and build the first version of the site
tasks.why: Everything below depends on it.
steps: Gathered public facts (facts.json), built the static site, forms backend, sync tools, tests and this HQ.
acceptance: `npm run build && npm test` pass

tasks.title: Get Clayton's go-ahead and answer the open questions
tasks.why: He owns the brand. Rule 1: nothing public or changed on his accounts without his OK.
steps: Show him the site (run `npm run dev` and open http://localhost:8080, or the preview from T05).
Walk through `facts.json` → `questions_for_clayton` and write his answers into the notes of this task.
Get a yes/no on each: brand spelling, using his first name, public email, domain choice, which platforms to claim.
acceptance: His approval is recorded in notes (date + how he said it)
Answers to every question are in notes

tasks.title: Decide who owns which account, and secure them
tasks.why: Domains, Cloudflare, email list and GitHub must be in Clayton's name with his email, or he can be locked out of his own brand.
steps: Create or confirm: a Clayton-owned Google/Gmail (or other) email for account sign-ups.
Use a password manager (1Password / Bitwarden) and turn on 2FA everywhere (authenticator app, not SMS where possible).
List any operator/helper accounts and give them delegated access instead of sharing passwords.
acceptance: Every account below lists Clayton as owner
2FA on registrar, Cloudflare, email list tool, GitHub

tasks.title: Register the domains
tasks.why: The website, email and every bio link need one home. Both spellings are unregistered today and could be taken any day.
steps: Re-check availability (facts.json is from 2026-10-07): `whois offtheripcollectables.com` should say 'No match'.
Open the registrar. Recommended: Cloudflare Registrar (sold at cost, free WHOIS privacy; needs a Cloudflare account). Alternatives: Porkbun, Namecheap. (verify current price)
Register `offtheripcollectables.com` (primary) and `offtheripcollectibles.com` (redirect). Optional: `offtheripcards.com`.
Turn ON: auto-renew, registrar lock, WHOIS privacy, 2FA.
Registrant email must be Clayton's.
acceptance: `dig +short NS offtheripcollectables.com` returns the registrar/Cloudflare nameservers
Auto-renew shows ON
Total spend ≤ $40
tasks.verify: Registrar prices and WHOIS-privacy policy change; read the checkout page before paying.

tasks.title: Put the project in a GitHub repository
tasks.why: Version history, collaboration between AIs, and automatic deploys.
steps: Human runs `gh auth login` once (browser).
In the project folder: `gh repo create off-the-rip-site --private --source . --remote origin --push` (private until launch; the repo contains no secrets).
Confirm `.gitignore` excludes `dist/`, `node_modules/`, `.env*`.
acceptance: Repo exists and `git log` shows the history online
No secrets in the repo (`git grep -iE 'api[_-]?key|secret' -- ':!*.md'` finds nothing real)

tasks.title: Deploy a preview to Cloudflare Pages
tasks.why: Lets Clayton see the real thing before any domain changes.
steps: Create a free Cloudflare account (T02 rules apply).

Option A (recommended): Workers & Pages → Create → Pages → Connect to Git → pick the repo. Build command `npm run build`, output directory `dist`, env var `NODE_VERSION=22`. Project name `off-the-rip`.
Option B (no Git): `npx wrangler login` (human approves in the browser) then `npm run deploy`.
Set `ALLOW_PAGES_DEV=1` and `ALLOW_NO_SINK=1` as variables on the preview so the forms don't error before T09/T10.
Open https://off-the-rip.pages.dev and click every nav link.
acceptance: Home, Shop, Pack Verdict, Watch, Want List, About, Links and the HQ path all load on the .pages.dev URL
Response headers on the HQ path include `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`
Lighthouse (Chrome DevTools) ≥ 90 on Performance, Accessibility and SEO for the home page

tasks.title: Clayton reviews the preview and lists corrections
tasks.why: Rule 1. He signs off before the real domain points here.
steps: Send him the .pages.dev link (not the HQ link).
Collect every correction in notes; fix; redeploy.
Get an explicit 'go' to connect the real domain.
acceptance: 'Go' recorded with a date

tasks.title: Connect the real domain and set redirects
tasks.why: Go live.
steps: Pages project → Custom domains → add `offtheripcollectables.com` and `www.offtheripcollectables.com`.
Redirect `www` → apex, and `offtheripcollectibles.com` → `https://offtheripcollectables.com` (Cloudflare Rules → Redirect Rules, preserve path).
Update `siteUrl` in `site.config.json` if different; `npm run build`; redeploy.
Check HTTPS padlock, and that `https://offtheripcollectables.com/sitemap.xml` loads.
acceptance: All four URL variants end on the primary https URL
Sitemap and robots load
The old preview URL is no longer used in any bio

tasks.title: Set up hello@ email
tasks.why: The site publishes hello@offtheripcollectables.com; mail to it must arrive.
steps: Cloudflare → Email → Email Routing → enable for the domain (adds MX + SPF automatically).
Create address `hello@` → forward to Clayton's real inbox; verify the destination via the confirmation email.
Optional: set up 'Send mail as hello@' in Gmail (needs an SMTP provider; (verify) options).
Send a test email to hello@ from a different account.
acceptance: Test email arrives
SPF record present (`dig TXT offtheripcollectables.com`)
tasks.verify: If Email Routing is unavailable, use any forwarding service; just don't publish an address that doesn't work.

tasks.title: Create the email list in Kit (ConvertKit)
tasks.why: The one asset eBay won't give him: a list he owns.
steps: Create a Kit account (free plan; (verify) current subscriber limit and terms).
Create a form named 'The Hit List'. Turn on double opt-in.
Create custom fields: source, interests, utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, want, budget, grade.
Settings → email: sender name 'Off The Rip Collectables', sender `hello@` once T08 works, and authenticate the sending domain (DKIM/SPF) per Kit's wizard.
Footer mailing address: Clayton chooses (PO box / virtual mailbox / home). Required by CAN-SPAM.
Create an API key (Developer settings) and note the numeric form id. Do not paste either into chat or the repo.
acceptance: Test signup on the preview shows up in Kit as an unconfirmed subscriber with the right fields
Footer address set
needs_human: Pasting the API key into Cloudflare (T10), not into any file
tasks.verify: The Kit v4 request shape in `functions/api/_lib.js` (POST /v4/subscribers, POST /v4/forms/{id}/subscribers, header X-Kit-Api-Key) was written from memory of the public docs. Check developers.kit.com before relying on it; fix `deliver()` if it differs.

tasks.title: Connect the forms and test end to end
tasks.why: A broken signup form silently loses customers.
steps: Cloudflare Pages → Settings → Variables and Secrets (Production): `SITE_URL=https://offtheripcollectables.com`, `KIT_API_KEY` (secret), `KIT_FORM_ID`. Optional: `FORM_WEBHOOK_URL` (Google Sheet backup), KV binding `LEADS`.
Remove `ALLOW_NO_SINK` from production.
Redeploy. Submit the home-page form with a real inbox, and the Want List form.
Confirm: Kit shows both subscribers with fields filled; the confirmation email arrives; a post with the hidden `website` field filled is silently ignored.
Command-line check: `curl -s -X POST https://<site>/api/subscribe -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"email":"you+test@example.com","consent":true}'` should return `{"ok":true}`.
acceptance: Real signup reaches Kit and the backup sink
Error path: with a wrong key the form shows an error instead of fake success
needs_human: Pasting secrets into the Cloudflare dashboard

tasks.title: Turn on privacy-friendly analytics
tasks.why: You can't improve what you can't see.
steps: Cloudflare → Web Analytics → add the site → copy the token.
Put it in `site.config.json` → `analytics.cloudflareToken` (a public token, not a secret). Optional: `analytics.plausibleDomain` for custom events (eBay Click, Newsletter Signup, Want List).
Rebuild, deploy, load a page, confirm a visit appears.
acceptance: Visits show in the dashboard
No cookie banner needed (no cookies set)

tasks.title: Register with Google Search Console and Bing
tasks.why: So the site and the Verdict pages get indexed.
steps: Search Console → Add property → Domain → verify with a DNS TXT record in Cloudflare.
Submit `https://offtheripcollectables.com/sitemap.xml`.
Bing Webmaster Tools → import from Search Console.
acceptance: Sitemap status 'Success' with 9 pages

tasks.title: Lock the HQ page behind Cloudflare Access
tasks.why: The HQ path is unlisted but anyone with the URL could read it. It contains planning notes, not secrets, but should still be private.
steps: Cloudflare Zero Trust (free for up to 50 users) → Access → Applications → Add → Self-hosted.
Application domain `offtheripcollectables.com`, path `backstage-otr26/*` (use the real `hqPath` from site.config.json).
Policy: Allow → emails: Clayton's and the operator's. One-time PIN login.
Confirm an incognito window gets the login screen.
acceptance: Incognito can't open the HQ page; both emails can
tasks.verify: Zero Trust free-plan limits and UI labels (verify).

tasks.title: Claim the X (Twitter) handle
tasks.why: The logo shows an X icon but no matching account exists, and the handle is free right now.
steps: Try `@offtheripcollectables` first. If taken, fallbacks in order: `@OTRCollectables`, `@offtherip_cc`, `@otr_cards` (check each in the signup flow; do not use names that other brands already use).
Sign up with the Clayton-owned email; phone verification is required.
Set the profile photo to `src/assets/img/logo-640.png`, bio from the Copy Kit, link to the site.
Put the final handle in `site.config.json` → `links.x` and rebuild.
acceptance: Handle exists, bio and link set, `links.x` filled so the footer shows it
tasks.notes: @OffTheRipCards and @offtheripco belong to other people. Don't confuse or impersonate.

tasks.title: Create a Facebook Business Page
tasks.why: Card buyers live in Facebook groups, and a personal profile can't run ads or hold a shop link.
steps: From Clayton's profile: Pages → Create. Name 'Off The Rip Collectables'. Category (verify): Collectibles Store or Trading Card Store.
Profile photo = the logo; cover = a banner (see T26); about text from the Copy Kit; website + eBay link.
Add a 'Shop now' / 'Learn more' button pointing at the eBay store.
Put the Page URL in `site.config.json` → `links.facebook`; rebuild.
acceptance: Page is public, has the logo, the bio and both links

tasks.title: Decide on Whatnot (live auctions)
tasks.why: Live selling is the biggest card-sales channel for many YouTubers; Clayton already makes video content.
steps: Ask Clayton whether he wants to go live weekly. If no, close this task.
If yes: apply as a seller at whatnot.com/sell; read current fees, payout and category rules (verify).
Set `links.whatnot` and `features.whatnotLive=true`, add the schedule to /watch/.
acceptance: Decision recorded; if yes, seller application submitted

tasks.title: Decide on TCGplayer (TCG singles)
tasks.why: TCG singles often sell faster on TCGplayer than eBay.
steps: Ask if he already sells there. If not, read the seller requirements and fee schedule (verify) and decide with Clayton whether the extra channel is worth the work.
If yes: set `links.tcgplayer`.
acceptance: Decision recorded

tasks.title: Make sure TikTok is live and cross-posting
tasks.why: TikTok is where card content grows fastest and the account exists but looks empty.
steps: Log in as Clayton; confirm the account is active; if empty, post the last 7 days of Shorts (download from YouTube Studio, no watermark issue).
Switch to a Business account if the 'website' field needs it (verify), set link = the site's /links/ page.
Set the bio from the Copy Kit; pin the best video.
acceptance: At least 7 posts live, bio link set

tasks.title: Unify every profile: name, picture, bio, one link
tasks.why: Every profile should look like the same business and send people to the same place.
steps: For each of YouTube, Instagram, Threads, TikTok, Facebook Page, X, eBay store: profile photo = `logo-640.png`; name 'Off The Rip Collectables'; bio from the Copy Kit; link = `https://offtheripcollectables.com/links/?src=<platform>` (ig, yt, tt, th, fb, x).
YouTube: Customize channel → Basic info → Links: add the website, eBay store, Instagram. Add the site to the About description.
Add the new website to the eBay store description and 'social links' if eBay offers it (verify; eBay restricts selling links but permits social and brand links).
acceptance: All profiles show the same name, logo and link
Links/redirects: `/yt`, `/ebay`, `/ig`, `/tiktok` resolve

tasks.title: Polish the eBay store itself
tasks.why: All sales happen here. Small store fixes lift conversion immediately.
steps: Seller Hub → Store: check whether the store URL slug (currently `offtheripollectables`, missing the 'c') can be changed; if not, leave it and use `/ebay` on the site. (verify)
Write the store description from the Copy Kit: what he sells, 'most cards pulled on YouTube', link to the channel.
Add store categories that match the site: Basketball, Football, Baseball, Pokémon, One Piece, Dragon Ball, Graded.
Add a banner/logo (logo-640.png).
Do not add links that sell outside eBay (rule 6).
acceptance: Store shows description, logo and categories
Seller Hub shows no policy warnings
tasks.verify: eBay store settings and link policy.

tasks.title: Switch on the live eBay inventory grid
tasks.why: The Shop page currently shows category shortcuts. Live listings with prices keep visitors on-site longer and send ready-to-buy traffic to eBay.
steps: developer.ebay.com → create a developer account (Clayton's) → Application Keys → Production keyset. Note the Client ID (App ID) and Client Secret (Cert ID).
GitHub repo → Settings → Secrets → add `EBAY_APP_ID`, `EBAY_CERT_ID`.
Locally: `EBAY_APP_ID=... EBAY_CERT_ID=... npm run sync:ebay`. Expect `ebay: N listings written`.
Check `src/data/listings.json` has `source: "ebay-api"` and sensible titles, prices, images.
`npm run build`, look at /shop/, commit.
acceptance: /shop/ shows a live grid with images and prices
Re-running the workflow refreshes it
needs_human: Creating the developer account, keyset approval (eBay may require a production-access review)
tasks.verify: `scripts/sync-ebay.mjs` follows the public Browse API docs but has NOT been run against live credentials. Fix the filter syntax / fields on the first run if the API differs.

tasks.title: Log the Daily Pack Verdict numbers
tasks.why: The scoreboard is the site's best retention hook. Days 17 to 23 show only win/loss; dollar amounts make the chart and totals appear.
steps: Clayton fills `templates/verdicts.csv` (cost and value for days 17 to 23) in a spreadsheet, or tells an AI the numbers.
`npm run import:verdicts -- path/to/verdicts.csv` → `npm run build`.
Going forward: log each new day (30 seconds) in the same CSV, or in the Kit/Sheet you prefer.
Define and publish the scoring method: what 'value' means (e.g. recent eBay sold prices for the cards pulled, minus fees?). Add 2 to 3 lines under the table in `src/pages/verdict.html`.
acceptance: /verdict/ shows dollar amounts, running chart and net total
A 'how we score' note is visible
tasks.notes: Auto-added days arrive with result=null (TBD) via `npm run sync:youtube`, which also breaks the streak until filled in.

tasks.title: Write the real About story and add a photo
tasks.why: People buy from people. The About page currently has only verified facts and no story.
steps: Clayton writes 3 to 5 sentences: why cards, how the channel started, what makes his rips different. Supplies a clear photo.
Add to `src/pages/about.html`, photo to `src/assets/img/`, then rebuild.
acceptance: About page has his story and photo (his approval recorded)

tasks.title: Confirm shipping, packing and returns, then publish them
tasks.why: Packing quality is the #1 trust signal for card buyers, but the site must only say what is true.
steps: Clayton describes exactly how cards ship (sleeve, toploader, team bag, bubble mailer? tracking? handling time?).
Write 3 to 4 bullets in the packing block of `about.html` and set `features.packingBlock` to `true`.
acceptance: Block live and accurate

tasks.title: Legal pass
tasks.why: Cheap insurance before collecting emails and running giveaways.
steps: Have someone competent review `privacy.html` and `terms.html` (they are plain-language templates, not legal advice).
Fill `legal.businessName` (and `legal.address` if you want it on the site).
Confirm giveaway practice: 'no purchase necessary', age and state limits, who is eligible, and FTC disclosure. Publish rules per giveaway.
Sales tax: eBay collects and remits for marketplace sales; selling anywhere else would change this (see rule 6).
acceptance: Review done; changes applied

tasks.title: Design the social images (OG image, banners)
tasks.why: The link-preview image people see when the site is shared is currently a basic placeholder.
steps: Render a 1200x630 image from an HTML template using the site fonts (headless Chrome screenshot) and save over `src/assets/img/og-image.jpg`.
Also produce a YouTube banner (2560x1440) and a Facebook cover (820x312) in the same style.
acceptance: Link preview looks right in https://www.opengraph.xyz/

tasks.title: Turn on the scheduled data refresh
tasks.why: Keeps the video grid, listings and Verdict stubs current without anyone touching the site.
steps: Cloudflare → My Profile → API Tokens → create a token with 'Cloudflare Pages: Edit' permission.
GitHub → Secrets: `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
Actions → refresh-and-deploy → Run workflow; confirm it passes and deploys.
acceptance: Workflow green; the site shows the newest video within 6 hours of an upload

tasks.title: Optimize the YouTube channel
tasks.why: All sales start here. Better packaging of the same content earns more views for free.
steps: Playlists: Daily Pack Verdict, Up or Down, Box & Blaster Breaks, Giveaways, Pokémon, One Piece, Sports.
Description template for every upload from the Copy Kit: what's in the video, eBay store link, website link, Verdict scoreboard link.
Pinned comment template; end screen pointing to the Verdict playlist; channel trailer = the best 60-second Verdict.
Thumbnails: consistent look (logo corner, big result 'PROFIT' / 'LOSS', the chase card). Test two styles for two weeks and compare click-through rate.
acceptance: Playlists and templates in place; CTR tracked in a sheet

tasks.title: Same-day cross-posting routine
tasks.why: Every Short already exists; posting it on 4 more platforms is the cheapest growth available.
steps: Same day: YouTube Short → TikTok → Instagram Reels → Facebook Reels → Threads (and X once claimed). Use the caption templates in the Copy Kit; same hashtags; bio link via `/links/?src=<platform>`.
Pick a scheduler if wanted (Buffer, Metricool, Meta Business Suite) (verify free tiers).
Track per-platform views weekly in the KPI sheet.
acceptance: 7 days in a row of cross-posts on all platforms

tasks.title: eBay listing optimization pass
tasks.why: The best traffic is already on eBay; better listings convert it.
steps: Titles: Year Brand Set Player Parallel /numbering Grade (use all 80 characters).
Photos: front + back, grading label, natural light; the first photo on a plain background.
Turn on Best Offer for singles; send offers to watchers; Promoted Listings Standard at a low ad rate for slow movers (verify rates).
Combined shipping / multi-buy discounts; sale events; relist unsold with a 5% markdown.
Add 'as seen on the channel' + video link in descriptions where the card was pulled (a link to YouTube, not an external store: rule 6).
acceptance: Sample of 20 listings updated; sell-through compared after 30 days
tasks.verify: eBay's current rules on description links and promoted listings.

tasks.title: Giveaway playbook
tasks.why: Giveaways already run on the channel; they are the main way to grow the list.
steps: Pick a repeatable format (e.g. every 25th Verdict Day, or per 100 subscribers).
Rules template (T25) in the video description; disclose any sponsor.
Mechanic: subscribe + comment to enter on YouTube. To build the email list, add 'get giveaway alerts: /giveaways/' as an extra, not a condition of entry (legal).
Announce winner on camera; ship the same week; post the proof.
acceptance: Next giveaway uses the template; list growth measured

tasks.title: Order inserts and (optional) 3D-printed stands
tasks.why: A small card in each order turns a one-time buyer into a follower. The filament photo suggests card stands could be a free gift or merch.
steps: Design a 3x5 insert: logo, 'Thanks!', QR code → `https://offtheripcollectables.com/thanks/?src=insert`, 'Watch the rips on YouTube'. Do NOT invite buyers to purchase off eBay (rule 6).
Print 500 (verify a vendor: Vistaprint, Moo, local).
If printing stands: test a slab-sized stand; photograph; decide free gift over $X vs. sold item on eBay.
acceptance: First 20 orders shipped with the insert; scans show up as `src=insert`
tasks.verify: eBay policy on inserts and promotional material in packages.

tasks.title: Build the welcome emails in Kit
tasks.why: Subscribers are warmest in their first week. Five emails, segmented by interest.
steps: Use `emails/welcome-series.md`. In Kit create a sequence; add conditions on the `interests` field for the sports / Pokémon / One Piece-DBS / graded variants.
Replace placeholders; send a test to Clayton; he approves the voice (rule 10).
Turn it on for new subscribers.
acceptance: A fresh test signup receives email 1 within a minute and the rest on schedule

tasks.title: Run the Want List like a service
tasks.why: A hunted card is a pre-qualified buyer. Keep the promise on the form.
steps: Weekly (Sunday): export the Want List (Kit custom fields or the backup sheet).
Search the store and the week's pulls; for each match, send a short email with the eBay link (the buyer buys on eBay).
Mark fulfilled; tell the buyer if nothing matches yet.
acceptance: First weekly pass done; reply rate and sales from matches tracked

tasks.title: Collect and publish real customer quotes
tasks.why: Social proof beyond the feedback score.
steps: Pick 5 positive eBay feedback comments.
Ask each buyer's permission by eBay message (only to ask permission to quote their public feedback, no sales message) (verify policy).
Add approved quotes to the About/Shop page.
acceptance: Quotes are real, permissioned and linked to the source

tasks.title: Retention loops
tasks.why: Return visits drive repeat buyers.
steps: Streak-break email: one automated email the day a Verdict ends the losing streak (subscribers who ticked interest 'verdict' come later; for now send manually).
Weekly 'Up or Down' price tracker for the featured card: log one price a week; add as a page (see Playbook → future builds).
Birthday-style 'anniversary' perk is overkill for now: skip until the list passes 500.
acceptance: Streak email sent the first time the streak breaks

tasks.title: Weekly routine (30 minutes)
tasks.why: Small, regular maintenance beats occasional big pushes.
steps: `npm run sync:youtube && npm run sync:ebay` (or let the Action do it).
Log the week's Verdict results (T22). Check Want List (T34).
Look at KPIs: YouTube subs, IG/TikTok followers, eBay followers, list size, site visits, eBay Clicks. Write them in the KPI sheet.
Send the weekly Hit List.
acceptance: KPI sheet updated every week

tasks.title: Monthly routine (45 minutes)
tasks.why: Keep facts accurate and the site healthy.
steps: Re-check facts.json numbers and update `stats` in site.config.json (with the new 'as of').
Run `npm test`; click every link; check domain/renewal dates; rotate API keys if anyone left the project.
Re-run the 'similar names' search (facts.json) to make sure no new lookalike brand appeared.
Review the Playbook and move the next 3 items into tasks.
acceptance: `stats.asOf` updated; no broken links
